idiom_name: Future { ... } + onComplete (Try[T] => U), Promise for external completion
implementation_notes: Future is the stdlib start-now/result-later type: Future { ... } begins evaluating immediately, and 'registering a callback is by using the onComplete method, which takes a callback function of type Try[T] => U' executed on an implicit ExecutionContext, while Promise completes a future explicitly when the outcome arrives from elsewhere. map/flatMap/recover compose callbacks, and blocking work should be isolated with blocking{} or a dedicated pool; choose this default when the surrounding codebase is Future-based.
code_sketch:
implicit val ec: ExecutionContext = ExecutionContext.global
val f: Future[Report] = Future { buildReport() }      // start now
f.onComplete {                                        // result later
  case Success(r) => publish(r)
  case Failure(e) => log.error("failed", e)
}
pitfalls: onComplete runs on an arbitrary pool thread from the implicit ExecutionContext: thread-local and UI state must be re-established inside the callback.
Future is eager - creating it starts the work - so 'start' and 'subscribe' cannot be separated, and callbacks registered after completion still run, immediately.
An exception thrown inside onComplete is reported to the ExecutionContext's reporter and lost, and blocking inside a Future without blocking{} can starve the pool.

variants.name: Effect system on fibers (Cats Effect IO / ZIO)
variants.idiom_name: cats.effect.IO (or ZIO) executed by IOApp, completion via attempt/flatMap
variants.implementation_notes: Effect systems replace Future+callbacks with a description of the computation: an IO[Report]/ZIO value is started by the runtime on a lightweight fiber, and completion handlers run in the effect context, so cancellation, resource safety and the error channel belong to the same abstraction ('purely functional effect system ... type-safe, composable asynchronous and concurrent programming'). Choose it where the whole program is effect-based; inside a Future-based codebase it is a heavyweight second model.
pitfalls: The effect is a description: nothing runs until the runtime executes it, so a 'start' that is never run or sequenced never happens.
Completion runs on the runtime's fiber pool; blocking must be declared (IO.blocking) or it starves the compute pool.
Mixing effect types (Future inside IO) reintroduces the eager, un-cancellable semantics the effect system exists to remove.
